text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller was given green light for Turkey's membership of the European Union by five of her European counterparts in her visit to Rome.
- Parliament will vote again on whether to investigate new corruption charges against Ciller because irregularities appeared in the first vote.

- Islamists compromise with coalition partners on the dress code banning the Islamist headscarf. Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party drops plans to lift the ban on civil servants but demands a change for university students.
- Far-rightist testifies to parliamentary commission that he and late gangster Abdullah Catli carried out attacks against Armenian guerrillas with official blessing.
- Italy accussed the visiting Ciller of having connections with heroin traffic in her official visit to Rome.
- A non-governmental organisation protests at the Islamist plan to erect a mosque in Istanbul's central Taksim Square.
- The last day to attend tender for the Akkuyu nuclear plant is Friday.
- Europe closes door to Turkey. Five foreign ministers meeting Ciller in Italy, do not see possibility for EU membership for Turkey for the time being.
